Make a master metadata dataframe adding the information for duration and dose
- but first, need to filter out those SRR in metadata_PFAS and metadata_ref for only duration == 1,10
- then we combine those two metadata files but need to configure that metadata_PFAS have the same columns - will need to add back duration and dose to it to continue

```{r}
# what columns are not the same between the metadata_{}

# colnames(metadata_ref)

# rename metadata_PFAS column so that it matches columns of metadata_ref
metadata_PFAS_final <- metadata_PFAS %>%
  rename('Library.Name' = 'GEO_Accession..exp.')

print('Whats in PFAS metadata_final, but not in ref metadata')
setdiff(colnames(metadata_PFAS_final),colnames(metadata_ref))

print('Whats in ref metadata, but not in PFAS metadata')
setdiff(colnames(metadata_ref),colnames(metadata_PFAS_final))
```

```{r}

count(metadata_ref, chemical, timepoint, dose)#, replicate)
min(count(metadata_ref, chemical, timepoint, dose)$n)
```

```{r}
# we need to drop some col or enter the missing data into the metadata from the index
metadata_ref_final <- metadata_ref %>%
  select(-c('cell_line','Collection_Date','geo_loc_name_country','geo_loc_name_country_continent','geo_loc_name','replicate')) %>%
  mutate(timepoint = as.numeric(sub("d", "", sub("24h", "1", metadata_ref$timepoint)))) %>%
  rename('duration' = 'timepoint') %>%
  mutate(chemical = ifelse(chemical == "DMSO", "DMSO_ref", chemical))

# put dose,timepoint into metadata_PFAS_final (from SRR_all)
# merge dose and timepoint by SRR
metadata_PFAS_final_merged <- merge(metadata_PFAS_final, SRR_PFAS, by='SRR', all=TRUE) %>%
  mutate(chemical = chemical.y) %>% # this so that we only have one chemical col (will be used by DESeq)
  select(!chemical.y) %>%
  mutate(chemical = ifelse(chemical == "DMSO", "DMSO_pfas", chemical))

ncol(metadata_PFAS_final)
ncol(SRR_PFAS)
sum(ncol(metadata_PFAS_final),ncol(SRR_PFAS))
ncol(metadata_PFAS_final_merged) # sum of both - the col used for the merge
```
```{r}
nrow(metadata_PFAS_final)
nrow(SRR_PFAS)
nrow(metadata_PFAS_final_merged)   # will be larger than both if there are unmatched SRRs on either side

head(metadata_PFAS_final_merged)
head(metadata_ref_final)
```


```{r}
# validate that both dataframes now have the same columns
print('Whats in ref metadata, but not in PFAS metadata')
print('should be nothing now because they should have same col now')
setdiff(colnames(metadata_ref_final),colnames(metadata_PFAS_final_merged))
setdiff(colnames(metadata_PFAS_final_merged),colnames(metadata_ref_final))


# make the master metadata dataframe combine metadata_PFAS_final with metadata_ref_final
metadata_all <- rbind(metadata_ref_final,metadata_PFAS_final_merged)

# validate that the sum of the 2 df is the merged
nrow(metadata_all) == sum(nrow(metadata_ref_final)+nrow(metadata_PFAS_final_merged))

```

Now, we need to reorder the columns of featurecounts to be the same as rows in metadata
"It is absolutely critical that the columns of the count matrix and the rows of the column data (information about samples) are in the same order. DESeq2 will not make guesses as to which column of the count matrix belongs to which row of the column data, these must be provided to DESeq2 already in consistent order."
https://bioconductor.org/packages//release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html#quick-start

```{r}
ncol(markdups_counts)
nrow(metadata_markdups)
# colnames(markdups_counts)
```
```{r}
# make sure that col of counts is in the same order as rows in metadata file
markdups_counts_aligned <- markdups_counts[
  match(colnames(markdups_counts), metadata_markdups$SRR)]
# match(x, table) — for each value in x, finds its position in table
#returns a vector of row-positions in metadata_PFAS_filtered_joined corresponding to each column name, in order


# colnames(markeddups_counts) now must be identical to metadata)markups
# for deseq to run
identical(colnames(markdups_counts_aligned), metadata_markdups$SRR)
```

### Create DESeq2 dataset
design = ~ chemical + duration

tests exactly your question: is there a significant difference in expression between PFBS and DMSO, with duration's effect on expression accounted for/adjusted out (since duration varies across both groups and would otherwise add noise to the comparison). Dose stays out for the reason we covered — it's confounded with chemical since DMSO doesn't span a dose range.
"does PFBS (averaged/pooled across whatever doses were tested) differ from DMSO?"
It's not asking "does PFBS at a specific dose differ from DMSO,"
```{r}
# dds = DESeqDataSet
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = markdups_counts_aligned, # sample gene counts unnormalized
  colData = metadata_markdups, # metadata info about samples
  design = ~ chemical
  # design = ~ chemical + duration # only works if have all durations?
)
dds
```

DESeq2 recommends removing any gene with less than 10 reads across all samples
https://rnabio.org/module-03-expression/0003/03/03/Differential_Expression-DESeq2/

**smallestGroupSize**: minimum number of samples for the same chemical, dose, and duration in metadata

For one gene row, if the total number of samples (columns) with gene counts of 0 is less than 3, for example, then we remove that gene
```{r}
# Pre-filtering: Remove low count genes
# dds <- dds[rowSums(counts(dds)) > 0, ] #10
# head(dds)

smallestGroupSize <- min(count(metadata_markdups, chemical, dose)$n) # smallest replicate number
# keep <- rowSums(counts(dds) >= 10) >= smallestGroupSize # original
# keep <- rowSums(counts(dds, normalized=TRUE) > 0) >= smallestGroupSize
keep <- rowSums(counts(dds) > 0) >= smallestGroupSize
dds <- dds[keep,]
```

Running the differential expression pipeline
https://master.bioconductor.org/packages/release/workflows/vignettes/rnaseqGene/inst/doc/rnaseqGene.html#differential-expression-analysis
```{r}
# running the differential expression pipeline
dds <- DESeq(dds) 
# extracts the estimated log2 fold changes and p values for the last variable in the design formula

# build results table
results <- results(dds)
results <- results[order(results$padj), ]
head(results)
```
```{r}
coef_name <- resultsNames(dds)[length(resultsNames(dds))]
resLFC <- lfcShrink(dds, coef=coef_name, type="apeglm")
head(resLFC)
```
```{r}
# Create Gene List for gsea based on results (not results lfc shrink)
gene_list <- results$stat # extract the stat column
names(gene_list) <- rownames(results) # add row names into this df gene_list
gene_list <- gene_list[!is.na(gene_list)] # remove na stat rows
rnk_df <- data.frame("SYMBOL" = names(gene_list), "STAT" = gene_list) %>% arrange(desc(STAT))
```
```{r}
head(rnk_df)
sum(duplicated(rnk_df$SYMBOL))
```

Finding the factor causing within-group separation (AI)
```{r}
pca_obj <- prcomp(t(assay(vsd)))
pc_scores <- as.data.frame(pca_obj$x[, 1:5])  # top 5 PCs
metadata <- as.data.frame(colData(vsd))

# for categorical variables, use ANOVA
# summary(aov(pc_scores$PC2 ~ metadata$batch))
# 
# for continuous variables (e.g. RIN score), use correlation
# cor.test(pc_scores$PC2, metadata$RIN)
```
```{r}
# 1. dose - most likely real driver of within-group variance
cor.test(pc_scores$PC2, metadata$dose)

# 2. sequencing depth
cor.test(pc_scores$PC2, metadata$Bases)

# 3. processing date as a coarse batch proxy
metadata$batch_date <- as.Date(metadata$create_date)
summary(aov(pc_scores$PC2 ~ metadata$batch_date))
```

```{r}
ggplot(tbl, aes(reorder(pathway, NES), NES)) +
      geom_col(aes(fill=padj<0.05)) +
      coord_flip() +
      labs(x="Pathway", y="Normalized Enrichment Score",
           title="Hallmark pathways NES from GSEA") + 
      theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
tbl <- table # convert table to data frame
tbl <- tbl[order(padj)] # sort by most significant first

topPathwaysUp <- tbl[ES > 0][head(order(pval), n=10), pathway]
topPathwaysDown <- tbl[ES < 0][head(order(pval), n=10), pathway]
topPathways <- c(topPathwaysUp, rev(topPathwaysDown))
fgsea::plotGseaTable(pathways[topPathways], ranks_list, tbl, 
              gseaParam=0.5)
```
